label: 2026-09-06 manual-worker insanity point
population_semantics: manual runs are assigned by started_at; archive time never moves an old-format run across the boundary

score_semantics.component_formula: weight * clamp((baseline-current)/baseline, -1, 1); all scored components are lower-is-better
score_semantics.important: diagnostic trend only; the worse axis is the headline so mechanically cheaper reporting cannot mask worse operational behavior; never a worker target, completion gate, scheduler input, product acceptance signal, or run-length incentive

guardrails: Tool-interval duration is shown but is not directionally scored; longer is not automatically better.
Always show both friction and operational axes, component values, and sample count with the headline delta.
Do not claim improvement before the post-boundary sample gate is met.
The headline is the worse of the two axes; friction reduction cannot offset operational degradation.
The score measures manual-reporting/process behavior, not model intelligence, user wellbeing, product quality, or MCP health.

friction.semantics: Measures reporting overhead directly changed by PR #658; useful as friction evidence but insufficient by itself to claim sanity improved.

operational.semantics: Measures downstream workflow pathologies not mechanically reduced merely by deleting report fields.
